questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to improve my written and spoken English

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That they spoke English as their first language, I wanted to live in a big city with a lot of culture, and I wanted to explore new ways of understanding academics

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite difficult because Goldsmith's webpage is not updated. Especially, it was very difficult for me to find the modules they offered. When the module selection came, it appeared to be other modules than those identified on the webpage. Furthermore, you were allowed to change them upon arrival and choose modules, which you weren't allowed to do at first. When you arrive, check out the new module selection platform, as they have a lot more to offer.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The study abroad team is sweet and helpful when you finally get an answer from them. I would recommend doing your exchange in autumn and not spring, as they have a lot more information, orientation and events at the beginning of the autumn semester. I thought there was a little of those arrangements in the spring semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Everything will work out. Is i maven! They are quite sweet to re-organise things even when the deadline is very close or over.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A lot of different options. I chose the cheapest one, Loring Hall. Would recommend that as most study abroad students do that. Your flatmates will be other international students and not British students, which is nice because you have the same circumstances - no friends and family and new to a foreign country

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I shared a kitchen with 9 others. It was small but ok as the Americans mostly prepared their meals in the microwave.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is easy, convenient, and it will be the people you will spend most time with. I hope you will get a good and social kitchen as I did.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't know if Unikit was worth the money, as I did not get my package on the day I arrived. The reception kindly had a duvet I could borrow, but no the ideal first day. Would recommend saying that you want the package delivered one day in advance upon arrival, and then just notify the reception by mail about this. IKEA in Greenwich is quite close to the campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Very confusing. Had to register multiple different places with systems that did not speak to each other, also upon arrival. I had difficulties with my wifi even though it was eduroam and I did not have wifi for a whole weekend. Again - is i maven! In the end it will all be sorted.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Study abroad team, but only by mail, and they were sometimes very slow at responding. If it is very urgent, I would recommend sending more emails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was quite successful in registering for classes, but not the ones I wanted in the beginning, because Goldsmith's webpage is not updated at all. It turned out to be two good classes anyway.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: As I described earlier, check out the module selection when you arrive. There is so many more modules to choose from and you have up to two weeks to change them after the begining of the semester! Just remember to send a new 'meritgodkendelse' to KU and be sure that they will accept the new modules as you cannot change them after the two weeks.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level is the same as at the University of Copenhagen, though you don't have to read as much - instead, the classes are more active. I didn't struggle with following along.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Classes were small, more discussion, and everyone knew the professor or tutor, as it was called. It was really nice, and I came more prepared and felt that I learned a lot more because you had to be active.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sociological Exhibition Making - 30 credits 
Cultural Studies and Capitalism - 30 credits

Two great courses which challenged the way we taught things at KU. They taught me to think in new academic ways.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: 'Sociological Exhibition Making' as you did a little research project and turned it into an exhibition for the broader public. You learn how to communicate academics to people other than academics.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: London is expensive, so if you want to do something and take trips outside London, make large personal savings

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was actually cheaper than expected. Also, public transport. Museums were free. There are just so many things to do in London that you easily spend a lot of money, because you want to explore.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are a lot of societies if you are interested - both creative and sports clubs. However, you have to do your research before and be outgoing.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Explore Trashy Tuesday and Sip and Paint. Visit the SU café!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to museums because there are a lot and they are mostly free! Explore New Cross, Peckham and Brockley in daylight - cute areas with a lot of nice cafes, shops, etc. My favourite café is called Sienna, where you have a view over the Thames. However, do it in daylight as Goldsmiths is placed in quite an unsafe area, so watch out for your surroundings. 

Go on hiking trips to the Seven Sisters or the Cotswolds. Explore Telegraph Hill Upper and Lower Park and enjoy the view (remember to get pizza from the local pizzeria)! Go to Nunhead Cemetery! Go to pubs, do a pub quiz and get a Sunday Roast! Try your local pubs out like Nunshead (AMAZING!), Rose, Marquise, The Dog and Bell, Skehans, etc. Oh, don't forget to explore Greenwich!!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy as you always understand what is going on due to everyone speaking English. Anyways, try to make an effort in understanding English culture. E.g. when the sun is shining, you go out to M&S to get Picky Bites, and when it is someone's birthday, you buy them the cake 'Collin the caterpillar'. It is fun to understand and live in a new culture!!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk with them in your classes and attend societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Goldsmiths is not as organised as UCPH. Is i maven! New Cross and the surrounding areas are not nice to walk in alone at night, so watch out. Try to always go home with other people.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture and classes with high participation

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Pubs are places to hang out with friends and even professors. You don't need to be drunk every time you walk into one. Order a lime and soda, which is 'danskvand med citron.' 
2. Goldsmiths is not as organised as UCPH, so 'hav is i maven' 
3. New Cross can be dangerous at night, so be careful 
(4. Everytime yoy want to do something in London, it takes at least 40 minutes from Loring Hall!) 
(5. No one is a pro at English - even the Brits make mistakes, so just speak!! They are just amazed by the fact that you can do this whole exchange in your second language!)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at my previous answers.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being more confident in English and getting new insights into how academics can differ

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That Goldsmiths is not as organised as UCPH

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Enjoy your visit!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
